about: Every kind of environment Afterprompt looks for before it scans anything. An environment is one filesystem with its own home folder and its own AI tool history: a key pasted inside a WSL distribution or a devcontainer is invisible from the machine hosting it. The scan reports on every kind listed here — found and scanned, found and not scanned with the reason, or not present — so the coverage section answers "what about X?" without anyone having to ask.

kinds.label: This machine
kinds.note: The filesystem the scan runs on.

kinds.label: WSL distributions
kinds.note: Each distribution has its own home. Scanned from inside itself, because reading it from Windows over \\wsl.localhost is about fourteen times slower.

kinds.label: Docker containers
kinds.note: A container has its own home folder, so an assistant run inside one — a devcontainer is the usual case — keeps its transcripts where the host cannot see them. The AI tool folders are copied out read-only; nothing is executed inside the container.

kinds.label: Podman containers
kinds.note: Same as Docker, through the podman CLI.

kinds.label: Docker images
kinds.why: An image is a filesystem nobody has typed into: it holds no conversation history, which is the only thing this tool looks for.
kinds.note: A key baked into an image layer is a real problem and a different tool's job: this one reports credentials that reached an assistant.

kinds.label: Dev container configuration
kinds.note: The configuration says a container exists; the container itself is scanned as a Docker container when it is running.

kinds.label: GitHub Codespace
kinds.note: A Codespace is the machine the scan is running on, not another environment to reach.

kinds.label: Lima or Colima virtual machines
kinds.why: Reachable only over its own ssh, which Afterprompt does not do yet.
kinds.note: Colima is where Docker usually runs on a Mac, so its containers appear under Docker instead.

kinds.label: Multipass virtual machines
kinds.why: Reachable only over its own shell, which Afterprompt does not do yet.

kinds.label: Other accounts on this machine
kinds.why: Reading another account's files needs elevation, and Afterprompt never elevates.
kinds.note: Listed so the coverage is honest about whose history was not read.

kinds.label: Extra home folders
kinds.note: A mounted disk or a fixture, scanned through the same worker protocol a distribution uses.
